question: In 2015 the ATLAS detector saw an excess of photon pairs at 750 GeV, a one-in-10,000 fluke at that mass. What became of it?
options: It was traced to a faulty cable
answer: It vanished. One in 10,000 was the chance of a fluke at 750 GeV alone; the search had scanned many masses and widths, and a bump that size somewhere was about a 1-in-50 event. Data from 2016, nearly four times as much, showed nothing there, after months of theorists racing to explain it.
move: A fluke somewhere is far likelier than a fluke right here.
trap: Treating one-in-10,000 odds as too rare to be chance.
